name: Spring Begins
description: Astronomical spring begins with the March equinox. The Sun crosses the celestial equator, and daylight and nighttime are nearly equal in length.
details: As the Northern Hemisphere moves into spring, days gradually become longer and temperatures generally begin to rise. Plants start growing, flowers bloom, and many animals become more active.

name: Summer Begins
description: Astronomical summer begins with the June solstice, when the Northern Hemisphere receives its longest period of daylight of the year.
details: The Sun reaches its highest apparent position in the sky at midday. After the solstice, daylight gradually becomes shorter, although summer weather typically continues for several months.

name: Autumn Begins
description: Astronomical autumn begins with the September equinox, when the Sun crosses the celestial equator moving southward.
details: Daylight gradually decreases across the Northern Hemisphere. Temperatures generally begin to cool, and many trees change color before shedding their leaves.

name: Winter Begins
description: Astronomical winter begins with the December solstice, which brings the shortest day and longest night of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.
details: The Sun reaches its lowest apparent midday position in the sky. After the solstice, daylight gradually increases, even though cold winter weather continues.
